messages:
jordan: ISP did a silent modem swap overnight and now my home server and cameras are unreachable. WAN IP is in 100.64.x.x so looks like CGNAT. router LEDs are judging me. pic: https://img.example/desk-cable-chaos.jpg
amy: Yikes. Which ISP? Some of them push CGNAT on new firmware.
devon: 100.64.x.x is the giveaway. Quick check: `curl -s ifconfig.me` or `curl -s icanhazip.com`.
jordan: Ran that: `curl -s ifconfig.me` -> 100.64.12.9. Their 'support' chat said "thats normal" and suggested factory reset. No bridge mode visible in UI.
sahil: Factory reset won't change carrier NAT. Short-term: request a public/static IP or put your own router behind theirs and use DMZ. GL.iNet or small OpenWRT box works well.
olga: Temporary hack: use Tailscale/ngrok/Cloudflare Tunnel for quick remote access to the cameras while you sort the ISP. I use Tailscale for my doorbell.
amy: Also if your new modem has an "ISP mode" or "passthrough" it's often buried in advanced settings. Sometimes ISPs lock it down though.
jordan: Ordered a GL.iNet travel router to run as edge and will set up Tailscale as fallback. Will post my config and before/after cable cleanup pics tomorrow desk is currently a spaghetti 7/10. :sweat_smile:
devon: Please post the reno pics and the router model. Might steal the setup. :grin:
sahil: And if you want, I can paste a quick `iptables` + DMZ snippet that I use for camera VLANs. Also set static DHCP for camera MACs so IPs don't jump.
jordan: Yes to all. Appreciate the help. Off to buy more cable ties and coffee. :coffee:
